column1: # Carrier inventory for the canonical persisted block_signatures_simplex_pq#13 BOC,
# the generated node/lite SignatureSet encodings, and complete node finality and
# lite forward-proof answers. Design section 6.5's node and lite gates are the
# ctests. Their names describe their subjects rather than the execution stage.
# The complete node/lite rows are measured by those gates through the real generated
# serializers, the exact admission predicates used by Plumtree and ADNL framed TCP,
# and the checked receiving parsers. This proves deliverability, not block acceptance
# or lite chain advancement, and does not stand up live overlay/TCP actor graphs.
# The generated signature-set measurements below corrected a projection
# that had invented 4 * signers + 4 bytes of bare-vector framing. The correction does not
# reopen the persisted envelope: that bound came from the #13 BOC plus BlockProof overhead,
# and the corrected network encodings are smaller.
# Lite-gate implementer note: despite the design text mentioning RLDP max_answer_size, this tree's
# production lite client uses AdnlExtClient::send_query over framed TCP and does not use RLDP on
# this path. The gate therefore boxes an adnl.message.answer and uses the external-connection
# packet admission shared with that route.
# The broadcast semantic gate measures the complete compressed-V2 production object at all four
# structural counts; 21 and 100 additionally pass trusted cryptographic verification.
# layer columns: kind, route, layer, operation, source, named_constant, recorded_bytes, observation
# minimum columns: kind, route, expected usable object bytes
# verdict columns: kind, object/signers, measured_or_projected_serialized_bytes, carrier_layer,
